kit_pier.text: Hey! Wow, you got here! I'm doing a live stream. Say hi to the viewers. All twelve of them.

sailor.text: The ferry to Douglas leaves whenever the tide agrees. Fancy a trip across?

rail_guard.text: Lime Street. Mind the gap. And mind the seagulls.

liver_bird_fan.text: Up on the Liver Building sit two Liver Birds, Bella and Bertie. One looks over the city, one over the sea.
Legend says if they ever fly away, the city will cease to exist. Don't tell them there's a gull strike.

beatles_fan.text: The Beatles played the Cavern Club nearly 300 times between 1961 and 1963. Mostly lunchtimes.
That's one every other day, nearly. Meanwhile I can't even manage a Tuesday.

dock_historian.text: Albert Dock opened in 1846. It was the first dock complex in the world built without any wood, so no fires.
Now it's all museums and tea rooms. Same bricks, fewer rum barrels.

verger.text: Liverpool Cathedral is the largest cathedral in Britain. Took seventy-four years to build, from 1904.
The tower's the highest of any cathedral. Do not try to dust it.

scouser.text: Scouse is a stew of beef, veg and spuds. The name comes from 'lobscouse', a sailor's meal.
We named ourselves after the stew. Not the other way round. Probably.

ferry_fan.text: Gerry and the Pacemakers sang 'Ferry Cross the Mersey' in 1964. Everyone on the boat has to hum it. It's the law.
The ferry's older than the song. And better at turning.
